criteria.name: Product specificity
criteria.notes: Reference conditioning is explicitly not implemented; exact product identity cannot currently be tested.

criteria.name: Output quality
criteria.notes: Publisher supplies complete encoded runs and stage-level numerical comparisons, but AIVP has not inspected a controlled output.

criteria.name: Control and consistency
criteria.notes: Prompt, seed, sampler, attention, patch and LoRA controls are documented; repeatability is untested.

criteria.name: Workflow strength
criteria.notes: Three-command setup and native MP4/WebM output are documented; Blackwell-only setup and no HTTP server limit workflow fit.

criteria.name: Speed and reliability
criteria.notes: One publisher MP4 run took 86.29 seconds and one WebM run 90.88 seconds; no average or AIVP failure-rate evidence.

criteria.name: Cost efficiency
criteria.notes: Code and weights are downloadable, but suitable hardware, energy and accepted-output cost are unresolved.

criteria.name: Commercial rights
criteria.notes: Engine is MIT; model license applies in Australia and disclaims MiniMax rights over outputs, with territorial, attribution, disclosure and use restrictions.

criteria.name: Automation and integration
criteria.notes: A reproducible CLI exists, but HTTP serving and MCP/API pathways are not implemented.

criteria.name: AU creator/SMB fit
criteria.notes: Australia is not excluded by the model license, but Blackwell hardware and 55GB model storage are poor indie-creator fit.

criteria.name: Monetization fit
criteria.notes: No affiliate or partnership program found; editorial demand is unmeasured.

analysis: A differentiated framework-free MiniMax H3 runtime with native media output and useful publisher benchmarks, but currently T2VA-only, Blackwell-bound and untested by AIVP.
confidence_notes: Primary repository, model package and license evidence only; no AIVP run.
